why: 1.8: the reasoning ("not 23 independent findings", the LD block, "rank and plausibility pointed in different directions", "so neither can be connected…") is already in Discussion §3 ¶3, so the Results keep only the facts: 23 genes in 12 loci, 7 in one locus. 2.1d: the two-stage selection is now one sentence in Sariel's form ("The 45 genes were functionally annotated and a final biological-relevance screen kept only genes with…"); "significance was the gate" is implicit, since only the 23 were screened. 5.1: the 61- and 53-word sentences are gone. The Discussion is not changed.
old: The 23 significant genes were not 23 independent findings: they fell in only 12 loci, and genes within a locus lie in the same linkage-disequilibrium block. A single locus, the 1.73 Mb fiber locus on chromosome 3H, contained seven of the 12 significant fiber genes. Among the 23, statistical rank and biological plausibility pointed in different directions: the most significant gene of the analysis (*HORVU.MOREX.r3.6HG0619810*, starch, *q* = 5.5 × 10⁻¹¹) returned no functional call from Swiss-Prot, InterPro or NCBI nr, and the second (*HORVU.MOREX.r3.3HG0301210*, fiber, *q* = 1.1 × 10⁻⁹) carried a transposase-derived domain, so neither can be connected to its trait through its function. Genes were therefore carried forward in two stages: significance in the haplotype analysis was the gate, and among the genes that passed it a biological-relevance screen kept only those with a documented or plausible role in the biosynthesis, transport or regulation of the corresponding grain component, rather than those ranking highest by significance.
